institution: NVIDIA; Stanford University; University of Texas at Austin

policy.baseModel: GR00T N1.7 with one Test-Time Training layer added to each of its 16 action DiT layers; each fast model is a two-layer MLP.
policy.modelSize: The action DiT grows from 538M to 690M parameters; this excludes the full vision-language backbone.
policy.inputs: Long sensorimotor histories, current visual observations / robot state and optional human-video or robot demonstration context, up to 8,000 timesteps.
policy.outputs: Continuous robot actions from the context-conditioned action model; fast weights encode the preceding trajectory.
policy.trainingData: Context-scaled pretraining plus task-specific post-training. Three real tasks have 8, 6 and 5 hours of collected data respectively, with online correction / DAgger-style distillation.
policy.trainingTime: 30,000 pretraining steps with gradually increased context length; post-training has task-specific schedules.
policy.trainingHardware: 16 NVIDIA GB200 GPUs per pretraining run; eight GB200 GPUs per post-training run; RTX 5090 inference workstation.
policy.controlRate: 30 Hz real-robot control in the reported deployment; 8,000 timesteps cover roughly five minutes at this rate.
policy.trainingMethod: Slow model weights are learned offline; fast weights are updated by gradient descent during both training and inference. Pretraining freezes the original GR00T components; post-training fine-tunes all parameters.
policy.evaluation: Three long-horizon real assembly tasks, including a ten-stage task; human-video one-shot imitation and on-the-fly improvement studies.

release.notes: The paper is public; implementation and artifact availability require separate verification.

evidence.label: Primary paper, full text
evidence.note: Publication date is the first arXiv submission. Policy fields distinguish model calls, controller execution and learning.

caveats: Inference updates fast weights, so this is not a strictly frozen-parameter attention-only ICL policy.
The 690M count is for the augmented action model, not the complete foundation policy.

summary: A causal video-action policy uses a human video prompt to specify manipulation tasks absent from robot post-training.

policy.baseModel: Human-video in-context world-action model. Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, separate causal video/action Transformers coupled through MoT, Wan VAE and T5.

policy.inputs: Robot RGB observation and state with either human video context or a language instruction.
policy.outputs: Joint future robot video and executable action chunks; action decoding attends to predicted future robot video.
policy.trainingData: Task-diverse VA pretraining corpus and HumanGen: 74,200 human-robot pairs covering approximately 8,600 tasks; synthetic semantically aligned human videos supplement robot trajectories.
policy.trainingHardware: 64 GPUs for RoboTwin post-training; GPU model not reported.
policy.controlRate: Not reported
policy.trainingMethod: Video/action flow matching with multi-horizon intermediate future prediction; all parameters fixed during unseen-task inference.
policy.evaluation: Seven held-out RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and physical insertion, multi-object and long-horizon manipulation.

name: ReCAP
title: Retrieve, Don't Retrain: Extending Vision Language Action Models to New Tasks at Test Time
summary: A residual world-action policy retrieves inexpensive cross-embodiment state-action chunks, allowing new tasks to be added to a frozen-policy retrieval pool.

policy.baseModel: Retrieval-conditioned residual world-action policy. Cosmos Predict2.5 2B / Cosmos Policy; DINO visual descriptors and SAM3-assisted object features for retrieval.
policy.modelSize: 2B base video model; complete policy count not reported.
policy.inputs: Current RGB, proprioception and task/object descriptors; retrieved observations, states and actions in a shared end-effector action space. Training retrieval additionally uses future query actions, removed at deployment.
policy.outputs: 16-step residual action chunks over retrieved actions plus future-state prediction; execute one step before re-retrieval.
policy.trainingData: RoboTwin: 246 target/pool paired training episodes across five tasks; separate PushT triangular target/disc-pusher pool data.
policy.trainingTime: 20,000 training iterations; wall-clock duration not reported.
policy.trainingHardware: 8 GPUs, per-GPU batch 16 with four gradient accumulation steps; GPU model not reported.
policy.controlRate: Not reported
policy.trainingMethod: Train the retrieval-conditioned residual policy once, then extend indexed pool trajectories without model updates.
policy.evaluation: PushT unseen target angles, five held-out RoboTwin tasks with progressively expanded UR5 retrieval pool, and real cross-embodiment manipulation.

release.notes: Released implementation, checkpoint and data are explicitly PushT scoped; complete RoboTwin/physical release is not established.

name: Universal Planning Networks

summary: Differentiable latent-space planning is trained through an inner trajectory optimizer and transfers goal representations to new robot control problems.

policy.baseModel: Inference-time counterfactual recovery wrapper. Frozen π0/π0.5, X-VLA, GR00T and OpenVLA variants; calibrated 3D observation synthesis rather than a learned video world model.

summary: Self-collected robot trajectories iteratively improve an in-domain visual planner while a frozen internet video prior supplies broader motion guidance.

policy.baseModel: Self-improving visual planning with inverse dynamics. Small in-domain video diffusion model, frozen AnimateDiff/SparseCtrl prior and inverse dynamics; optional distilled Diffusion Policy.

policy.trainingData: MetaWorld in-domain initialization uses eight seen tasks with 25 demonstrations/task; each improvement iteration collects 30 new trajectories. Real experiments cover cup pushing and drawer opening.
policy.trainingTime: In-domain initialization: 70,000 MetaWorld or 88,000 Panda steps. Per iteration: 10,000 MetaWorld, 8,000 cup-pushing or 10,000 drawer steps; wall time not reported.

policy.controlRate: Evaluates open-loop, per-action replanning and intermediate control schedules; a single universal Hz is not reported.
policy.trainingMethod: Inverse probabilistic adaptation combines internet and in-domain visual models; robot interaction updates in-domain video and inverse-dynamics weights.
policy.evaluation: MetaWorld novel tasks and physical Panda cup pushing/drawer opening, with optional language-ordered multi-cup extension.

An EMA target branch supplies noised future slot features, while an auxiliary interaction head predicts pairwise proximity-and-motion relations. The displayed losses are noise prediction, slot VICReg, relation BCE, and assignment entropy. (b) Previous slots query current point tokens through competitive assignment, weighted aggregation, and residual refinement, repeated three times per frame. (c) Two observed point clouds and the robot state produce slot condition tokens for the diffusion policy, which predicts the action sequence using cross-attention and FiLM.

Figure 2: Overview of UniWALM .
UniWALM is a unified mixture-of-transformers (MoT) world-action-language model that co-denoises video, language, and action in a single shared representation.
Given the current observation, task instruction, proprioception, an optional visual memory ℱ \mathcal{F} (one or more frames; in our experiments a single anchor at episode start), and the previously generated textual memory , UniWALM processes inputs through a (a) video , (b) language , and (c) action DiT that share features via unified self-attention.
The language stream emits a subtask together with a textual memory string, which is re-consumed as the prompt on the next control step, closing a language-as-memory loop across time. Video generation is disabled at inference, so the language and action DiTs run without producing future frames.

During exploration, the agent compiles its perception and planning logic into standalone Python control programs that execute high-frequency loops directly on the robot. imageCandidates.note:
Fig. 1: Overview of RoboCasa-Shift. RoboCasa-Shift evaluates VLA robustness on selected long-horizon RoboCasa tasks under controlled single-factor distribution shifts with multiple frozen severity levels.
Strictly matched clean-perturbed rollouts enable counterfactual comparison under shared task conditions, while robustness is characterized jointly through end-to-end task outcomes and stage-aware semantic execution diagnostics.
Representative findings illustrate that aggregate success rates can mask substantial episode-level outcome changes, similar end-to-end degradation can correspond to different failure locations, and severe visual corruption can shift failures toward earlier stages of task execution.
